original_value: The estimation of PMx (incl. PM10 and PM2.5) concentrations using satellite observations is of great significance for detecting environmental issues in many urban areas of north China. Recently, aerosol optical depth (AOD) data have been being used to estimate the PMx concentrations by implementing linear and/or nonlinear regression analysis methods. However, a lot of relevant research based on AOD published so far have demonstrated some limitations in estimating the spatial distribution of PMx concentrations with respect to estimation accuracy and spatial resolution. In this research, the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform is employed to obtain the band reflectance (BR) data of a large number of Landsat 8 Operational Land Imager (OLI) remote sensing images. Combined with the meteorological, time parameter and the latitude and longitude zone (LLZ) method proposed in this article, a new BR (band reflectance)-PMx (incl. PM10 and PM2.5) model based on a multilayer perceptron neural network is constructed for the estimation of PMx concentrations directly from Landsat 8 OLI remote sensing images. This research used Beijing, China as the test area and the conducted experiments demonstrated that the BR-PMx model achieved satisfactory performances for the PMx-concentration estimations. The coefficient of determination (R2) of the BR-PM2.5 and BR-PM10 models reached 0.795 and 0.773, respectively, and the root mean square error (RMSE) reached 20.09 μg/m3 and 31.27 μg/m3. Meanwhile, the estimation results have been compared with the results calculated by Kriging interpolation at the same time point, and the spatial distribution is consistent. Therefore, it can be concluded that the proposed BR-PMx model provides a new promising method for acquiring accurate PMx concentrations for various cities of China.

result.paraphrase: Estimating PMx concentrations, including PM10 and PM2.5, from satellite observations is highly important for identifying environmental problems in many cities across northern China. Although aerosol optical depth (AOD) data have recently been used to estimate PMx levels through linear and nonlinear regression methods, prior AOD-based studies have shown limitations in both estimation accuracy and spatial resolution when mapping PMx distribution. In this study, the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform was used to extract band reflectance (BR) data from a large number of Landsat 8 Operational Land Imager (OLI) remote sensing images. Together with meteorological data, time parameters, and the latitude and longitude zone (LLZ) method proposed here, a multilayer perceptron neural network was built to create a new BR-PMx model for directly estimating PMx concentrations from Landsat 8 OLI imagery. Beijing, China served as the test area, and experiments showed that the BR-PMx model performed satisfactorily in PMx concentration estimation. The coefficient of determination (R2) reached 0.795 for BR-PM2.5 and 0.773 for BR-PM10, while the root mean square error (RMSE) was 20.09 μg/m3 and 31.27 μg/m3, respectively. The estimated results were also compared with Kriging interpolation results at the same time point, and the spatial patterns were consistent. Thus, the proposed BR-PMx model offers a promising new approach for obtaining accurate PMx concentrations in cities throughout China.
